creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Seen 2026-11-09 on 0.24 on the laptop, with the devenv attached to the window. An agent ran `muster pane new --helper --name review-codex`, which printed the callsign `fiddle`. `muster msg post --to fiddle` then refused: "fiddle could be p2jgfgnd1j or fiddle@devenv; say which". The callsign `pane new` had just returned could not be used as given; posting to the pane id worked.

e2822dd4 has the window tell each daemon which callsigns the other machines hold, and the daemon passes over them. A pane made by `muster pane new` from the CLI carries no such list: `callsigns_elsewhere` is always empty there (crates/muster-daemon-proto/src/making.rs, "Nothing that asks without a window sees another machine's panes"). Agents make most helpers this way, often while a window that knows the other machine's callsigns is attached.

Possibly: have the daemon keep the last list a window sent it and pass those callsigns over for CLI-made panes too. Or have `pane new` print a ref that reaches the new pane alone, such as its pane id, when the bare callsign is shared.
title: `pane new` from the CLI hands out a callsign another machine's pane holds
